newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares finish sharply weaker.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares finish sharply weaker.

text.p: Zimbabwe industrial shares closed Monday more than 100 points weaker but dealers said any further losses this week were unlikely to be as sharp.
The most notable feature of trade on Monday was a two-one share split in Delta Corporation. The share closed at 1,450 cents.
Generally, volumes were moderate and most trade remained mixed with interest shown by both local institutions and foreigners.

"It was pretty slow today. Volumes were middle-of-the-road. It's still underpinned by local institutions so the index won't drop sharply again. This is probably about as sharp as it will drop all week," one dealer said.
"The locals are still showing a bit of interest and the foreign investors are coming in for bits and pieces," he added.
The 57-share industrial index finished 110.53 points weaker at 9,896.09 -- dropping below the key 10,000 point level for the second time in less than a week.
Dealers said that the industrial index was weighed by FMB which shed 300 cents to 5,700 cents, Finhold which lost 40 cents to 730 cents and Alloys which was 80 cents weaker at 570 cents.
Barclays rose 25 cents to 3,225 cents and Radar added 60 cents to 460 cents.
The seven-share mining index inched up 1.14 cents to 886.84 cents in quiet trade. Falcon and Falgold were unchanged, while Wankie put on five cents to 505 cents.
